claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on MML-1 localization and lifespan in different longevity mutants.

claims.claim: Mammals harbor four hexokinases that differ in tissue expression, subcellular localization, and affinity to glucose and G6P.
claims.source: Mammals harbor four hexokinases that differ in tissue expression, subcellular localization, and affinity to glucose and G6P.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mammalian hexokinases.

claims.claim: HXK-1 was expressed in the cytosol of neurons, pharynx, gonadal sheath, and coelomocytes.
claims.source: We found that HXK-1 was expressed in the cytosol of neurons, pharynx, gonadal sheath, and coelomocytes (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: HXK-2 had a reticular expression pattern in neurons, muscle, intestine, and hypodermis.
claims.source: HXK-2 had a reticular expression pattern in neurons, muscle, intestine, and hypodermis (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: HXK-3 signal was diffused and highly expressed in the pharynx, muscle, hypodermis, and intestine.
claims.source: HXK-3 signal was diffused and highly expressed in the pharynx, muscle, hypodermis, and intestine (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Full-length HXK-2 strongly co-localized with mitochondria.

claims.evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Mitochondrial localization of HXK-2 was abolished entirely in the d10 HXK-2 mutant that lacks the first 10 amino acids after the initiator methionine.

claims.claim: Hexokinases are differentially expressed in C. elegans.
claims.source: In summary, we found that hexokinases are differentially expressed in C. elegans and identified HXK-2 as the worm mitochondrial hexokinase.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the tissue expression data in Figure 2A, B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: HXK-2 is the worm mitochondrial hexokinase.
claims.source: In summary, we found that hexokinases are differentially expressed in C. elegans and identified HXK-2 as the worm mitochondrial hexokinase.
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-localization data in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: MML-1 localized with mitochondria in the intestine.
claims.source: Hence, we crossed the MML-1::GFP strain with the mitochondrial reporter TOMM-20::mCherry under the intestinal promoter ges-1 and confirmed that MML-1 localized with mitochondria in the intestine (Figure 2D and E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2D and E.

claims.claim: Under normal conditions, around 60–80% of the total MML-1 was nuclear, and 15% co-localized with mitochondria.
claims.source: Under normal conditions, around 60–80% of the total MML-1 was nuclear, and 15% co-localized with mitochondria.

claims.claim: MML-1 mitochondrial localization was increased to ~62% of total MML-1 upon hxk-2i.

claims.evidence: This is supported by co-localization analysis in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Upon hxk-2 knockdown, MML-1 is excluded from the nucleus and re-localizes to a subset population of mitochondria.

claims.claim: Increased expression of hsp-6::GFP was observed upon knockdown of mitochondrial components ogdh-1, sucl-1, and sucl-2, as well as in control worms treated with antimycin A.

claims.claim: Inducing mitochondrial stress with AA did not affect MML-1 nuclear localization under control conditions and hxk-2 knockdown.

claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Exposure to paraquat induced the oxidative reporter gst-4p::GFP.

claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: Exposure to paraquat did not affect MML-1 nuclear localization at the concentrations tested.
claims.source: however, we did not see any effect on MML-1 nuclear localization at the concentrations tested (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claims.claim: MML-1 regulation by glucose metabolism genes is independent of mitochondrial and oxidative stress.

claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on mitochondrial stress and oxidative stress.

claims.claim: Increased total lipid storage was observed under hexokinase knockdown in the wild-type and glp-1(e2141) backgrounds.

claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H.

claims.claim: No difference in basal OCR was found under hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in the wild-type background.

claims.claim: glp-1(e2141) animals showed decreased basal OCR compared to wild type.

claims.evidence: This is supported by OCR data in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: hxk-1 and mml-1 knockdown significantly increased the basal OCR compared to glp-1(e2141).

claims.evidence: This is supported by OCR data in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: A greater percentage of OCR reduction upon adding etomoxir was observed under hxk-1 knockdown in wild-type and hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in glp-1(e2141).
claims.source: Interestingly, we saw a greater percentage of OCR reduction upon adding etomoxir under hxk-1 knockdown in wild-type and hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in glp-1(e2141) (Figure 2I), indicating higher mitochondrial β-oxidation levels.
claims.evidence: This is supported by OCR data in Figure 2I.

claims.claim: Higher mitochondrial β-oxidation levels were indicated under hxk-1 knockdown in wild-type and hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in glp-1(e2141).
claims.source: Interestingly, we saw a greater percentage of OCR reduction upon adding etomoxir under hxk-1 knockdown in wild-type and hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in glp-1(e2141) (Figure 2I), indicating higher mitochondrial β-oxidation levels.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the OCR data in Figure 2I.

claims.claim: Increased expression of acs-2p::GFP was found upon hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown.
claims.source: We confirmed this result using the transcriptional reporter acs-2p::GFP, a mitochondrial acyl-CoA synthase that is induced and required for fatty acid β-oxidation in C. elegans (Van Gilst et al., 2005), and found increased expression upon hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I.

claims.claim: MML-1 nuclear localization was rescued upon acs-2i under hxk-1i.

claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2J.

claims.claim: acs-2i did not rescue MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-2i.
claims.source: Interestingly, acs-2i did not rescue MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-2i.
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2J.

claims.claim: Etomoxir supplementation rescued MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-1i, but had no effect upon hxk-2i.
claims.source: We also pharmacologically inhibited fatty acid oxidation by supplementing etomoxir and again saw the rescue of MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-1i, but no effect upon hxk-2i (Figure 2K).

results.result: An RNAi screen of glucose metabolic enzymes identified hexokinases (hxk-1 and hxk-2) as the most vigorous regulators of MML-1 nuclear localization, with knockdown of most glycolytic and TCA cycle enzymes decreasing MML-1 nuclear accumulation, while knockdown of PPP enzymes increased it.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C4, C22-C28 provide converging evidence from the RNAi screen (Figure 1A-B, Supplementary file 1) showing differential effects of glucose metabolism enzyme knockdown on MML-1 localization. The screen methodology appears sound with appropriate controls (luci RNAi), multiple replicates (N≥2), and validation in two independent reporter strains (C31). The interpretation (C29-C30) is reasonable given the data pattern.

results.result: Hexokinase activity drives MML-1 nuclear translocation, as demonstrated by pharmacological inhibition with 3-BrP and 2-DG, with hxk-1 and hxk-2 showing specific effects without cross-reactivity or confounding effects on food consumption or development.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C37 demonstrate pharmacological validation of the genetic findings using two independent hexokinase inhibitors (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B-C). Claims C38-C44 provide important controls showing RNAi specificity (western blots), no effects on growth, feeding, motility, or mml-1 mRNA levels, ruling out major confounders. The convergence of genetic and pharmacological evidence with appropriate controls strongly supports the conclusion.

results.result: Hexokinases are upstream regulators of MML-1 nuclear localization and transcriptional function in germline-mediated longevity, as hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown abolished MML-1 nuclear localization, decreased target gene expression, and suppressed glp-1(e2141) longevity without affecting wild-type lifespan.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C52 provide a logical progression from localization (Figure 1C-D) to transcriptional activity (Figure 1E) to lifespan (Figure 1F), with appropriate controls (wild-type lifespan unaffected). The data show statistical significance and multiple biological replicates. The epistatic relationship is clearly demonstrated, supporting the conclusion that hexokinases act upstream of MML-1 in this longevity pathway.

results.result: MML-1 requires HXK-1 and HXK-2 for germline and mitochondrial longevity (glp-1 and isp-1 mutants) but not for insulin and mTOR longevity (daf-2 and raga-1 mutants), indicating pathway-specific regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C60 systematically test hexokinase requirements across four longevity pathways with consistent methodology (Figure 1G-H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1L-P). The differential effects are clearly demonstrated with appropriate statistical analysis. However, the interpretation (C61) could benefit from additional mechanistic investigation to explain why some pathways require hexokinases while others do not.

results.result: C. elegans hexokinases are differentially expressed across tissues, with HXK-2 identified as the mitochondrial hexokinase based on co-localization with mitochondria and loss of localization upon deletion of the N-terminal 10 amino acids.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C67 provide clear microscopy evidence (Figure 2A-C) showing tissue-specific expression patterns and mitochondrial localization of HXK-2. The d10 mutant experiment (C67) provides strong functional evidence that the N-terminus is required for mitochondrial targeting. The conclusion (C68-C69) is well-supported by the imaging data.

results.result: Upon hxk-2 knockdown, MML-1 redistributes from the nucleus to mitochondria, with mitochondrial co-localization increasing from ~15% to ~62% of total MML-1.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C73 provide quantitative co-localization data (Figure 2D-F) using appropriate markers (TOMM-20::mCherry) and analysis methods (Manders' coefficients). The dramatic shift in localization is statistically significant and biologically meaningful. The imaging and quantification appear rigorous with multiple replicates (N=3).

results.result: MML-1 regulation by glucose metabolism genes is independent of mitochondrial and oxidative stress, as neither antimycin A-induced mitochondrial stress nor paraquat-induced oxidative stress affected MML-1 nuclear localization.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C77 provide appropriate positive controls (hsp-6::GFP and gst-4p::GFP induction) demonstrating that the stress treatments worked (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-G), yet MML-1 localization was unaffected. This rules out stress responses as the mechanism, supporting the conclusion (C78) that metabolic regulation is direct rather than stress-mediated.

results.result: HXK-1 regulates MML-1 nuclear localization by modulating mitochondrial β-oxidation, as evidenced by increased lipid storage, elevated β-oxidation markers, and rescue of MML-1 nuclear localization upon β-oxidation inhibition with acs-2 RNAi or etomoxir, specifically under hxk-1 but not hxk-2 knockdown.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C88 provide converging evidence from multiple approaches: lipid measurements (C79), OCR analysis (C80-C84), transcriptional reporters (C85), genetic epistasis (C86-C87), and pharmacological rescue (C88). The specificity for hxk-1 vs hxk-2 (C87, C88) is particularly compelling. The conclusion (C89-C90) that hexokinases regulate MML-1 through distinct pathways is well-supported by the differential rescue experiments.

results.result: HXK-2 regulates MML-1 by modulating the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), as hxk-2 knockdown increased NADPH levels and TKT-1 activity, while PPP inhibition rescued MML-1 nuclear localization and target gene expression under hxk-2 but not hxk-1 knockdown, independent of G6P levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C99 provide multiple lines of evidence: pharmacological PPP inhibition (C91), metabolite measurements (C92), enzyme activity assays (C93), genetic epistasis (C95-C96), transcriptional readouts (C97-C98), and G6P quantification (C99). The data consistently show that PPP inhibition specifically rescues hxk-2 but not hxk-1 phenotypes. The conclusion (C100-C101) that PPP activity regulates MML-1 independent of G6P is supported by the observation that rescue occurs despite low G6P levels.

results.result: Reducing PPP activity extends lifespan and rescues glp-1(e2141) longevity upon hxk-2 knockdown, placing PPP epistatically downstream of hxk-2 in the regulation of MML-1 function and longevity.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C106 provide lifespan data (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1J) showing that tkt-1 knockdown extends wild-type lifespan, has no additive effect with glp-1, and rescues the lifespan suppression caused by hxk-2 knockdown. The epistasis analysis is appropriate and supports the conclusion (C107-C108) about the pathway hierarchy. Statistical analysis appears adequate with multiple replicates (N=3).

results.result: Mass spectrometry analysis of MML-1 immunoprecipitates identified MXL-2 (known binding partner) and revealed enrichment for nuclear and mitochondrial proteins, as well as lipid droplet proteins including PLIN-1.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C112 describe the proteomics results (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C) with appropriate controls (non-transgenic wild-type) and biological replicates (N=3). Detection of the known binding partner MXL-2 (C109) validates the approach. The enrichment analysis appears sound, though the manuscript would benefit from more detailed statistical thresholds for defining 'enrichment.'

results.result: MML-1 localizes to mitochondria associated with lipid droplets (LDs), with co-localization significantly increased upon hxk-2 knockdown, as demonstrated using the LD dye LipiBlue and validated LD markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C117 provide systematic validation of LD visualization (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-F) followed by MML-1 co-localization analysis (Figure 4C-E). The use of LipiBlue is validated against established LD markers (DHS-3::GFP, PLIN-1::mCherry), and quantitative co-localization analysis shows statistically significant increases upon hxk-2 knockdown. The imaging and analysis appear rigorous.

results.result: PPP inhibition correlates with decreased LD size, and MML-1 nuclear localization rescue upon hxk-2 knockdown by PPP inhibition is associated with reduced LD size, while hxk-1 and hxk-2 show differential effects on LD metabolism, supporting distinct regulatory mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C118-C122 provide LD size measurements (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1H-I) showing differential effects of various knockdowns. The correlation between PPP activity, LD size, and MML-1 localization (C124-C125) is supported by the data, though the causal relationship could be more rigorously established. The differential effects of hxk-1 vs hxk-2 on LD metabolism (C122-C123) support the conclusion of distinct mechanisms.

results.result: LD metabolism regulates MML-1 nuclear localization, with dgat-2 knockdown increasing and atgl-1 knockdown decreasing nuclear MML-1, and epistasis analysis placing LD metabolism upstream or parallel to the PPP.
results.evaluation: Claims C126-C129 provide lipid measurements and localization data (Figure 4G-H, Figure 4—figure supplement 1J) showing that manipulating LD metabolism affects MML-1 localization. The epistasis experiment (C129) showing that tkt-1 knockdown rescues the atgl-1 phenotype supports the conclusion (C130) about pathway relationships. However, the 'upstream or parallel' conclusion is somewhat ambiguous and could benefit from additional experiments to distinguish between these possibilities.

results.result: Inhibition of the PPP rescues mammalian MondoA nuclear translocation and transcriptional function upon starvation in HEK293T cells, as demonstrated by increased nuclear localization and elevated expression of target genes TXNIP and ARRDC4.
results.evaluation: Claims C131-C134 provide evidence from mammalian cell culture (Figure 5A-D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-C) showing that 6-AN treatment increases MondoA nuclear localization and target gene expression under both high-glucose and starvation conditions. The use of two concentrations of 6-AN and multiple target genes strengthens the findings. The conclusion (C135) that PPP regulates MondoA is supported, demonstrating evolutionary conservation of the mechanism.

results.result: Background and context claims establishing the role of MML-1/MXL-2 and MondoA/ChREBP in longevity, metabolism, and aging.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C2, C12-C21 provide established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These claims set the context for the study but do not represent novel findings from this work. The citations appear appropriate and the background is accurately represented.

results.evaluation: These summary claims are supported by the detailed mechanistic data in claims C79-C90 (β-oxidation) and C91-C101 (PPP). The evidence is comprehensive and the conclusions are well-supported, but these are summary statements of results already evaluated in detail.

results.result: An RNAi screen of glucose metabolic enzymes identified hexokinases hxk-1 and hxk-2 as the most vigorous regulators of MML-1 nuclear localization. Knockdown of most glycolytic enzymes, pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, and most TCA cycle enzymes decreased MML-1 nuclear accumulation, while knockdown of certain TCA cycle enzymes (OGDC and SCS subunits) and PPP enzymes (T25B9.9 and tkt-1) increased MML-1 nuclear localization.
results.evaluation: All three reviewers affirm the screen findings without questioning the methodology or conclusions. Reviewer 1 states the evidence is 'convincing,' Reviewer 2 describes it as 'compelling evidence,' and Reviewer 3 notes 'the data support their proposed working model.' No concerns were raised about the RNAi screen results or the identification of hexokinases as key regulators.

results.result: Pharmacological inhibition of hexokinases with 3-BrP and 2-DG decreased MML-1 nuclear localization, confirming that hexokinase activity drives MML-1 nuclear translocation. Control experiments showed that hexokinase RNAi was specific to each isozyme and did not affect worm growth, pharyngeal pumping, motility, or mml-1 mRNA levels.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted these validation experiments without critique. The pharmacological confirmation and control experiments are treated as supporting evidence for the main findings. No reviewer questioned the specificity of the RNAi or the interpretation that effects are not due to developmental or feeding phenotypes.

results.result: In germline-deficient glp-1(e2141) mutants, hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown abolished MML-1 nuclear localization, decreased expression of MML-1 target genes (mdl-1, lgg-2, swt-1, fat-5), and suppressed the extended lifespan, while not affecting wild-type lifespan. This demonstrates that hexokinases are upstream regulators of MML-1 in germline-mediated longevity.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'The authors showed that knockdown of hxk-1 and hxk-2 suppressed longevity caused by germline-deficient glp-1 mutations' as part of the compelling evidence. All reviewers accepted these findings as demonstrating the role of hexokinases in germline longevity without raising concerns.

results.result: Hexokinase knockdown decreased MML-1 nuclear localization and abolished lifespan extension in isp-1(qm150) mitochondrial longevity mutants, but did not affect MML-1 localization or suppress lifespan in daf-2(e1370) insulin signaling mutants or raga-1(ok701) mTOR longevity mutants. This indicates MML-1 requires HXK-1 and HXK-2 for germline and mitochondrial longevity, but not for insulin and mTOR longevity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the pathway-specific requirement for hexokinases without challenge. The differential effects across longevity pathways are treated as valid findings that support the specificity of the hexokinase-MML-1 regulatory axis. No concerns were raised about these epistasis experiments.

results.result: Hexokinases are differentially expressed in C. elegans tissues. HXK-1 is cytosolic in neurons, pharynx, gonadal sheath, and coelomocytes. HXK-2 has a reticular pattern in neurons, muscle, intestine, and hypodermis and strongly co-localizes with mitochondria. A deletion mutant lacking the N-terminal 10 amino acids (d10 HXK-2) abolished mitochondrial localization, identifying HXK-2 as the worm mitochondrial hexokinase.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the tissue expression and subcellular localization data without critique. The identification of HXK-2 as the mitochondrial hexokinase through co-localization and deletion analysis is treated as a valid finding supporting the mechanistic model.

results.result: MML-1 localizes with mitochondria in the intestine. Under normal conditions, 60-80% of MML-1 is nuclear and 15% co-localizes with mitochondria. Upon hxk-2 knockdown, MML-1 mitochondrial localization increases to ~62% of total MML-1, indicating that MML-1 is excluded from the nucleus and re-localizes to a subset population of mitochondria.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'They found that genetic inhibition of hxk-2 changed the localization of MML-1 from the nucleus to mitochondria and lipid droplets' as part of the compelling evidence. The co-localization data and quantification are accepted without methodological concerns.

results.result: MML-1 regulation by glucose metabolism genes is independent of mitochondrial and oxidative stress. Inducing mitochondrial stress with antimycin A or oxidative stress with paraquat did not affect MML-1 nuclear localization under control conditions or hxk-2 knockdown.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted these control experiments demonstrating that the effects are not due to general stress responses. No concerns were raised about the stress induction experiments or the interpretation that MML-1 regulation is stress-independent.

results.result: Hexokinase knockdown increases total lipid storage and affects oxygen consumption. In glp-1(e2141) mutants, hxk-1 and mml-1 knockdown increased basal OCR, and greater OCR reduction upon etomoxir treatment indicated higher mitochondrial β-oxidation levels under hxk-1 knockdown. Expression of the β-oxidation reporter acs-2p::GFP increased upon hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the metabolic phenotyping data linking hexokinase knockdown to lipid metabolism and β-oxidation. These findings are treated as supporting evidence for the mechanistic pathway without methodological concerns.

results.result: Inhibition of β-oxidation rescues MML-1 nuclear localization specifically under hxk-1 knockdown but not hxk-2 knockdown. Both genetic (acs-2i) and pharmacological (etomoxir) inhibition of β-oxidation rescued MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-1i but had no effect under hxk-2i, suggesting HXK-1 promotes MML-1 nuclear localization by decreasing mitochondrial β-oxidation and that the two hexokinases regulate MML-1 through somewhat independent pathways.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'The authors demonstrated that genetic or pharmacological inhibition of hexokinases decreased nuclear localization of MML-1, via promoting mitochondrial β-oxidation of fatty acids' as compelling evidence. The differential rescue by β-oxidation inhibition is accepted as demonstrating distinct mechanisms for the two hexokinases.

results.result: Inhibition of the mitochondrial hexokinase HXK-2 enhances the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP). hxk-2i increased NADPH levels and TKT-1 enzymatic activity. Knocking down PPP enzymes (T25B9.9 and tkt-1) rescued MML-1 nuclear localization and target gene expression under hxk-2i but not hxk-1i, even with lower G6P levels, indicating that inhibiting the PPP is sufficient to rescue MML-1 function independent of G6P levels.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'They found that genetic inhibition of hxk-2 changed the localization of MML-1 from the nucleus to mitochondria and lipid droplets by activating pentose phosphate pathway (PPP)' as compelling evidence. The PPP activation data and rescue experiments are accepted without methodological concerns.

results.result: PPP inhibition extends lifespan and rescues glp-1(e2141) longevity upon hxk-2 knockdown. tkt-1 knockdown extended wild-type lifespan and had no additive effect in glp-1(e2141) background. Knockdown of T25B9.9 and tkt-1 rescued glp-1(e2141) longevity upon hxk-2i, indicating that increased PPP under hxk-2 knockdown suppresses MML-1 function and that reducing PPP restores longevity, placing PPP epistatically downstream of hxk-2.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the lifespan data and epistasis analysis demonstrating the PPP-longevity connection. The rescue of longevity by PPP inhibition is treated as strong evidence for the proposed pathway without concerns about the experimental design or interpretation.

results.result: Mass spectrometry analysis of MML-1 immunoprecipitation identified MXL-2 (an established binding partner) and revealed enrichment for nuclear and mitochondrial proteins, as well as proteins from different organelles including lipid droplets. PLIN-1, one of the most abundant LD proteins, was co-enriched in MML-1 IP.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the proteomics data identifying MML-1 interacting partners and organellar associations. The detection of PLIN-1 is treated as supporting evidence for MML-1's association with lipid droplets without methodological concerns.

results.result: MML-1 localizes to lipid droplets (LDs) and mitochondria associated with LDs. LipiBlue staining co-localized with LD-resident proteins DHS-3::GFP and PLIN-1::mCherry, validating it as a reliable LD visualization method. MML-1 localized with LipiBlue-positive structures and appeared at mitochondria associated with LDs. MML-1 co-localization with LDs significantly increased upon hxk-2 knockdown.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'MML-1 localized to mitochondria associated with lipid droplets (LD)' as part of the compelling evidence. The co-localization data using LipiBlue and the increased LD association upon hxk-2 knockdown are accepted without methodological concerns.

results.result: PPP inhibition affects lipid droplet size. tkt-1 knockdown significantly reduced LD diameter and total amount, while hxk-2i alone had no effect. Double knockdown of hxk-2 and tkt-1 resulted in smaller and fewer LDs. Knockdown of acs-2i and hxk-1i acs-2i double knockdown resulted in a mild but significant increase in LD size, supporting that the two hexokinases regulate MML-1 via distinct mechanisms.
results.evaluation: The Reviewing Editor notes 'they find that knockdown of acs-2 and hxk-1 acs-2 double knockdown each result in a mild but significant increase in LD size. This result supports that the two hexokinases regulate MML-1 via distinct mechanisms.' This was added in response to reviewer concerns and is now accepted as supporting the model.

results.result: MML-1 can localize with a specific subpopulation of mitochondria associated with lipid droplets, and inhibition of the PPP can rescue MML-1 nuclear localization upon hxk-2i correlated with decreasing LD size.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'MML-1 nuclear localization was correlated with LD size and metabolism' as part of the findings. The correlation between PPP inhibition, MML-1 rescue, and LD size changes is accepted as supporting the mechanistic model.

results.result: Lipid droplet metabolism regulates MML-1 localization. atgl-1i increased lipid levels and decreased nuclear MML-1, while dgat-2i increased MML-1 nuclear localization. MML-1 nuclear localization in atgl-1i was rescued upon tkt-1 knockdown, suggesting LD metabolism is upstream or parallel to the PPP in MML-1 regulation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the epistasis analysis linking LD metabolism to PPP and MML-1 regulation. The rescue of MML-1 localization by PPP inhibition in the atgl-1i background is treated as valid evidence for the pathway hierarchy.

results.result: In mammalian HEK293T cells, PPP inhibition with 6-AN decreased NADPH/NADP+ ratio and increased MondoA nuclear localization in both high-glucose and starvation conditions, without affecting MondoA transcript levels. Expression of MondoA target genes TXNIP and ARRDC4 increased upon PPP inhibition, indicating that the PPP regulates mammalian MondoA localization and transcriptional function.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'The authors further showed that the inhibition of PPP increased the nuclear localization of mammalian MondoA in cultured human cells under starvation conditions, suggesting the underlying mechanism is evolutionarily conserved.' All reviewers accepted the conservation of the mechanism without concerns about the mammalian cell experiments.
